necessary_context.content: Eq. (1) minimizes over X subset R^n and maximizes over Y subset R^m the expression f(x)+<Ax-b,y>-g(y). Eqs. (3) and (4) define phi and psi; Eq. (5) gives weak duality. The selected construction has g=0. Euclidean vector norms and spectral matrix norms are the default.
necessary_context.name: Saddle problem and gap

necessary_context.content: Eq. (7) returns the bundled exact triple (grad f(x),Ax,A^T y). Eq. (8) maps public data theta and the full previous Oracle transcript to both the next query pair and an approximate output pair, each in X times Y. The remaining data, including X,Y,g,b,Lf and the associated norm, may be known. No linear-span restriction is imposed on these rules.

necessary_context.content: Eq. (88) sets RX^2=k(2k+1)^2 and RY^2=k/4; Theorem 9 uses k=2t+4. These are not arbitrary independently prescribed radii. Eq. (88) visibly prints y in R^n, while the selected dual space is R^m as defined on p.2. Lemma 13's statement includes the endpoint t=(k-4)/2, whereas its printed induction uses strict inequalities in s; this potential Proof gap is recorded without a local repair.
